resources.string: Play games by tilting or turning your phone or head

Clu turns small movements of your device into touches and joystick drags in games, for people who find touch screens hard to use. It needs to perform gestures on your behalf and to see which app is in front, so it can pause itself in Settings and on the home screen. It also listens for keys you choose, such as a switch interface or volume buttons. Clu does not read what is on your screen.

If Android blocks turning Clu on ("Restricted setting"), do these steps in this order:
1. Tap Accessibility settings, find Clu (on Xiaomi and POCO under "Downloaded apps") and try to turn it on. When the "Restricted setting" message appears, tap OK.
2. Tap App info, then ⋮ (top right) › "Allow restricted settings", and confirm with your PIN or fingerprint. This menu item only appears after step 1.
3. Go back to Accessibility settings and turn Clu on.
Clu was installed from a file, so Android will ask for the extra steps below the first time.
Don\'t use \"Force stop\" or phone-cleaner tools on Clu: Android then switches its accessibility service off and you have to turn it on again.

Notifications: not allowed. Allow them to get Pause, Recenter and Stop in the notification shade.

Hold your device in your most comfortable position when you tap Start or Recenter. That position becomes \"center\".
To place the stick and buttons on a game\'s controls, open the game and tap Layout on the Clu panel.

HyperOS closes background apps aggressively. Set these once so Clu keeps working during games:
1. Battery saver › "No restrictions" (button below).
2. On the same page, turn off "Pause app activity" if you see it.
3. Autostart › allow Clu (button below).
4. Open Recents and lock Clu: pull its card down, or long-press it and tap the padlock.
5. Don't use Ultra battery saver while playing.
When you turn Clu on, Xiaomi shows a warning with a 10-second countdown before OK works. Wait for it, then confirm. A helper can make this first-time setup easier.

Game Turbo: in its Game DND settings keep \"Don\'t open notification shade\" off if you use Clu\'s notification buttons, and turn on \"Restrict screenshot gestures\". Names can differ slightly between versions.

For shooters. Choose \"Aiming\" under Motion controls, then put the aim pad on the game\'s look area with Layout. The aim moves only while you move, by as much as you move, and stops when you stop. Slow, small movements give slow, small aim corrections, and there is no speed to hold steady. Bind \"Switch moving / aiming\" to a twist, a sound or a switch to walk and aim with the same motion, and \"Precision aim\" for fine adjustments on a target.

Opens a test pad that stands in for a game. \"Synthetic test\" moves a virtual stick in circles and taps button A every 1.2 seconds, without using the motion sensors, to show whether this phone accepts Clu\'s touches. Share the report if something looks wrong.
Turn on \"Clu motion controls\" in Accessibility settings first.

Tap Synthetic test, or start a session and tilt. Green = finger down, white = up, red X = cancelled. While the test runs, touch the pad once with a real finger: you should see a red X, then a new green dot about a third of a second later.
